title: Constantine
objective: After this level you can explain Constantine's rise and his support for Christianity.
summary: Constantine won at the Milvian Bridge in 312 CE, gave Christians tolerance in 313, ruled alone from 324 and called the Council of Nicaea.

cards.headline: Ten years after the Great Persecution began, Christians were free to worship.
cards.body: What changed so fast? A new emperor, and a battle at a bridge.

cards.headline: The Milvian Bridge
cards.body: In 312 CE Constantine defeated his rival Maxentius at the Milvian Bridge outside Rome. Christian writers said he saw a sign before the battle and had his soldiers fight under a Christian symbol. Whatever he saw, he won. By 324 CE he had beaten his last rival too and ruled the whole empire alone. Diocletian’s rule of four had become rule of one.

cards.headline: A Christian-friendly emperor
cards.body: Then things moved fast. In 313 CE the Edict of Milan granted religious tolerance to Christians throughout the empire. Just ten years earlier, in 303 CE, Diocletian had launched the Great Persecution. In 325 CE Constantine went further and called the Council of Nicaea, a meeting of bishops that agreed a common statement of Christian belief. An emperor was now hosting the church’s biggest meeting.

cards.fact: Constantine was baptized only on his deathbed.
cards.context: The emperor who granted Christians tolerance and gathered the bishops at Nicaea was not baptized until 337 CE, as he was dying. He joined the church officially on his way out.

cards.headline: Constantine: crowned
learned: Constantine won at the Milvian Bridge in 312 CE
The Edict of Milan came in 313 CE
He called the Council of Nicaea

questions.prompt: What did the Edict of Milan grant in 313 CE?

options.label: A new capital in the East

questions.explanation: The Edict of Milan granted religious tolerance to Christians throughout the empire.

questions.prompt: Why was the Council of Nicaea important?

options.label: It ended the Tetrarchy by imperial law
Bishops agreed a shared statement of belief
It moved the Senate to the eastern capital

questions.explanation: In 325 CE the bishops at Nicaea agreed a common statement of Christian belief.

questions.prompt: From Level 43: like Constantine by 324 CE, who went from sharing power to ruling the Roman world alone?

options.label: Marcus Agrippa
options.rationale: He was Octavian’s admiral, not the ruler.

options.label: Lepidus
options.rationale: He shared power but never ruled alone.

questions.explanation: After Actium, Octavian was sole master of the Roman world, just as Constantine came to rule alone.
